approaches.name: Plain recursion
approaches.intuition: Compare the last characters and branch into replace, delete and insert when they differ. Subproblems repeat enormously.
steps: If the strings end with the same character, drop it from both
Otherwise take 1 + the best of three smaller problems
approaches.time: O(3^(n + m)) in the worst case: unusable for long strings

approaches.name: Dynamic programming over prefixes
approaches.intuition: Fill a table of distances between every pair of prefixes. Only the previous row is needed, so two rows suffice.
steps: Initialise the first row and column
Fill row by row using the three neighbours
approaches.space: O(min(n, m)) with two rolling rows
pitfalls: Off-by-one between string indices and table indices.
Matching characters cost 0 and take the diagonal value, never 1 + something.
Empty strings: the answer is the length of the other string.

talkTrackMd: Define the table, explain the three transitions as replace, delete and insert, and mention that the rolling-row version keeps the same O(n x m) time with far less memory.
